meta.note: written ten weeks into 2026 from the standings, the all-play Elo, the season simulation's odds (rerun with the 2026-11-17 week_odds fix, so Week 11 is priced on each team's best projected lineup), each roster's WAR pace (banked plus the rest of the projection, best legal lineup, taxi and IR excluded), and every trade since the Week 8 outlooks

2.head: 8-2 · Elo 1686 (2nd) · WAR pace +8.90 (1st) · playoffs 99.99% · title 39%
2.headline: No First-Round Pick Until 2030, and It's Working
2.text: Last time I said this front office went full Danny Ainge at the deadline. Wrong guy. Ainge is the one who ends up with the picks. Three more trades in three days last week (seven in four weeks, twelve this year), and the big one sent the 2028 and 2029 firsts to Baby Billys for Chris Olave. Add the 2027 first that already belongs to the Cockroach and this team doesn't make a first-round pick until 2030. That's the Nets trading for Pierce and Garnett, and I say that as somebody who enjoyed the other end of that deal. The defense: it's working. 8-2, first in WAR pace, 185 points last week, 94% for a bye, and the Lawrence-for-Lamar swap is officially a heist (Lawrence is on pace for 1.11 WAR, Lamar is on IR with a broken thumb). Two straight titles buys you the right to push every chip in. But Travis Kelce is the flex at 36, Christian McCaffrey is 30, and the sim has the title race at 39% to the Church's 38%. Week 13 against the Church decides the top seed. Flags fly forever. The bill shows up in 2028.

8.head: 7-3 · Elo 1696 (1st) · WAR pace +8.64 (2nd) · playoffs 99.9% · title 38%
8.headline: An 8-2 Team Wearing a 7-3 Costume
8.text: Three losses in four weeks, and I'm still not selling. The Church scored 148 and 160 in two of them, and the 160 came with Brock Bowers leaving early. Losing with 160 on the board is a Stomach Punch game, the kind you're still muttering about in the shower on Wednesday. Look at the whole picture: first in points, first in Elo, 90-20 in all-play (the best record in the league against the field), and the most points against of anybody. This is an 8-2 team wearing a 7-3 costume. Here's what bugs me. Bijan al-Gaib has made seven trades in four weeks. The Church has made zero since August 5. Part of that is the cupboard, with no first or second until 2029. But Bryce Young is on the bench on pace for 0.84 WAR while three bubble teams start Jacoby Brissett, 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers and Michael Penix in the superflex. That's a seller's market, and Chase Brown (on pace for 0.55) is still the flex. Make one call. Week 13 against Bijan al-Gaib is for the top seed, and it might be a preview of the final.

6.head: 7-3 · Elo 1668 (3rd) · WAR pace +7.03 (3rd) · playoffs 93% · title 8%
6.headline: The Hottest Team in the League Just Lost Puka Nacua
6.text: The hottest team in the league just lost its best player, so it's time to find out if Puka Nacua has a Ewing Theory. Four straight wins, including the Church, Bijan al-Gaib and a 194.86 that went down as the fourth-highest score in league history. Then Nacua and Michael Wilson went to IR next to De'Von Achane. Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 and Wilson is done for the year too. Nacua has MCL and PCL sprains plus turf toe, and the earliest he can come back is Week 15, the first week of the playoffs. That's the optimistic version. The first game without Puka was a 138-75 win over the Tenders, which proves nothing, because the Tenders started Tua. The real test is the schedule: MOORE this week, then Bijan al-Gaib, Drake Mungo and the Church, and the sim has Jeantrification as the underdog in all of the last three. That's how a 7-3 team that's third in Elo and third in WAR pace is 93% to make the playoffs and 8% to win it, down from 17% two weeks ago. Rashee Rice (on pace for 0.31 WAR) is the WR3 now. The fix is sitting in the drawer: the 'Doza's 2027 second, which should land around 15th overall, plus the 2029 first. Spend them on a receiver. And again: nearly 300 points left on the bench, the most in the league. Stop it.

1.head: 6-4 · Elo 1608 (4th) · WAR pace +6.99 (4th) · playoffs 53% · title 4%
1.headline: From 86% to 53%, With the Top Three Still to Come
1.text: Two weeks ago I told this team to trade Kirk Cousins. Then Drake Maye hurt his ankle on the first drive in Munich last week and might be done for the year, which makes Cousins, now Minnesota's quarterback, the superflex for as long as this season lasts. So ignore me. Sometimes the best trade is the one you don't make. Everything else got worse. The five-game winning streak ended with a loss to the Cockroach as an 85% favorite, and playoff odds that were 86% a week ago are 53%. Now look at what's left: Bijan al-Gaib, the Church, Jeantrification, then Bijan al-Gaib again. That's the top three teams in the league, one of them twice, after ten weeks of facing the fewest points of anybody. The bill always comes. Trey McBride (on pace for 1.40 WAR, the best tight end in the league) and Brock Purdy are real. The receivers are six guys you've heard of (Jefferson, London, Evans, Diggs, Metcalf, A.J. Brown) and none of them is in the top eleven at the position. Brown left that Munich game with a hamstring injury too. Mike Evans just cost two more seconds, and the 2027 and 2028 firsts are already gone. The best chip left is the Tenders' 2028 first. Keep it. This isn't the year.

11.head: 6-4 · Elo 1573 (6th) · WAR pace +6.52 (5th) · playoffs 64% · title 2%
11.headline: You Can't Win These Two Games With Keenan Allen
11.text: I said the schedule printed half of this record and that the next opponents wouldn't all score 60. The next two scored 151 and 185. Both losses, by 33 and 60. So that held up. It's still 6-4 and 64% to make the playoffs, because Jaxon Smith-Njigba has banked 1.40 WAR, the most of any player in the league, and Matthew Golden is a real second receiver. After that it gets thin fast. Keenan Allen is the WR3 at 34, on pace for 0.06 WAR. Jacoby Brissett is the superflex. Kyler Murray got benched, Terry McLaurin is out for the year, and Tyreek Hill is still an unsigned free agent rehabbing his knee. That's a lot of 2022 on one bench. Here's what kills me: three receivers changed teams last week. Chris Olave cost two firsts, fine. But Mike Evans went for two seconds and DJ Moore went for one, and this team is still holding every 2028 and 2029 pick it was born with. This week JSN and Golden are both on bye against the Cockroach (21% to win), and the Cockroach comes back around in Week 14. The season is those two games. You can't win them with Keenan Allen.

3.head: 6-4 · Elo 1479 (8th) · WAR pace +5.30 (7th) · playoffs 65% · title 3%
3.headline: The Cockroach Is in the Tyson Zone. Now Buy a Receiver
3.text: I called this team the cockroach of the league, and it changed its name to the Un-killable Cockroach. I've never been prouder of anything I've written. Then it lost to Jeantrification by 100.86, the kind of loss that gets a coach fired at halftime, and came back a week later to beat Drake Mungo as a 15% underdog behind 43.5 from George Pickens. This team is in the Tyson Zone now. Nothing it does can surprise me. The numbers still say be careful: eighth in Elo, seventh in WAR pace, seventh in points, exactly 55-55 in all-play, and somehow 6-4 and 65% to make the playoffs. Kenneth Walker (on pace for 1.39 WAR) and Patrick Mahomes are carrying a lineup where Wan'Dale Robinson is the WR3, on pace for 0.03. Zero point zero three. Here's the thing: no bubble team is better set up to buy. Bijan al-Gaib's 2027 first, its own 2028 and 2029 firsts, five seconds, and since its own 2027 first already belongs to the 'Doza, losing buys nothing. Shough My Hock twice in the next four weeks, the first time without JSN. Buy a receiver this week and finish the job.

9.head: 5-5 · Elo 1596 (5th) · WAR pace +6.34 (6th) · playoffs 64% · title 5%
9.headline: The Best-Run Lineup in the League Still Needs a Quarterback
9.text: Still the unluckiest team in the league, and now it's getting dangerous. Fifth in Elo, 69-41 in all-play, second-most points against, and 5-5. Then last week it beat the Church as a 13% underdog with three starters on bye, because Jahmyr Gibbs (on pace for 1.93 WAR, the best of any player in the league) scored 44 and the lineup went against the projection with Xavier Hutchinson over Rhamondre Stevenson and was right. That's the part I love. This team has left 143 points on the bench all season. Nobody else is under 175. It's the best-run lineup in the league. Which makes the quarterback thing so maddening. I said buy one two weeks ago. Nothing. Matthew Stafford at 38 and Michael Penix are 16th and 25th among quarterbacks in WAR pace, they're both on bye this week, and every first through 2029 is still sitting in the drawer next to five seconds. Bryce Young is on the Church's bench. Geno Smith is on Bijan al-Gaib's. After Baby Billys this week it's Shough, the Cockroach and the Nix pics, the three teams it's fighting for a spot. The sim gives this a 5% title shot at 5-5, fourth-best in the league. Pick up the phone.

10.head: 5-5 · Elo 1487 (7th) · WAR pace +5.22 (8th) · playoffs 17% · title 0.3%
10.headline: 4-0 to Start, 1-5 Since, and Time to Sell Derrick Henry
10.text: This is the Behind the Music episode, and we're at the part where the narrator says it all fell apart. 4-0 to start. 1-5 since. The last three weeks: 113, 83 and 85 points, the worst stretch of any team that still has playoff odds. Last week Caleb Williams and Bo Nix were both on bye, Shedeur Sanders put up a 0.0 at quarterback, and Deebo Samuel scored 25.9 on the bench while Germie Bernard started and scored 1.0, a 24.9-point mistake in a game lost by 21.2. Seventh in Elo, eighth in WAR pace, eighth in points, 17% to make the playoffs. And tanking doesn't work either, because the 2027 first belongs to the Tenders, who are thrilled about all of this. So what's left? Derrick Henry is 32 and still on pace for 0.79 WAR. He's worth more to a contender over the next month than he'll ever be worth to this team again. Sell him for a 2027 pick, get back into that draft, and see what happens against the Tenders, the Cockroach, Shough and Captain Jah'Merica. Still one trade all year, and it was in August. The phone works both ways.

7.head: 5-5 · Elo 1399 (9th) · WAR pace +4.12 (9th) · playoffs 45% · title 0.9%
7.headline: The Luckiest 5-5 Team Has a Path to 9-5
7.text: The team formerly known as Hampton Inn traded a 2027 second for DJ Moore and renamed itself MOORE, in all caps, which is also what this lineup needs at seven positions. I told this team to sell Josh Allen. It won three straight and bought a receiver instead. Scoreboard. For now. Allen (on pace for 1.58 WAR) and Joe Burrow (1.51) are the two best quarterbacks in the league. The other seven seats combine for about 1.05 WAR of pace, a little less than Dak Prescott by himself. This is 41-69 in all-play, ninth in Elo, ninth in points, and it finished dead last in scoring two straight weeks in October. It's the luckiest 5-5 team I can remember. But look at the schedule: Jeantrification this week (33% to win), then the Tenders, the 'Doza and Baby Billys, the three worst teams in the league, as a big favorite in all three. Win this week and 9-5 is on the table. Lose and it comes down to tiebreakers, and the tiebreaker is points, where this team is ninth. One more thing: the 2027 first belongs to the 'Doza, so there's no prize for missing. Go get one more receiver.

4.head: 2-8 · Elo 1277 (11th) · WAR pace -1.21 (12th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
4.headline: The Full Hinkie: Eight Firsts and a Lineup Below Replacement
4.text: Two weeks ago I said pick a lane. Baby Billys picked one and drove it off a cliff, on purpose, and I mean that as a compliment. Chris Olave, the best player on the roster, went to Bijan al-Gaib for the 2028 and 2029 firsts. This is the full Hinkie now: eight first-round picks and six seconds over the next three drafts, four of the firsts in 2027, with Lamar Jackson (broken thumb, six to ten weeks) and Jalen Hurts (out for the season) on IR waiting for next year. And the best lineup this team can field is on pace for -1.21 WAR. Negative. As a team. Tommy DeVito is the quarterback. Last week it scored 53.84 points, the fourth-lowest total in league history, and lost. Here's why that matters: draft order in this league goes by max points, so you can't tank by benching guys. You have to actually be bad. Mission accomplished, with the lowest max in the league and the inside track on the 1.01. The catch is that the other three 2027 firsts come from Jeantrification, the Church and Shough My Hock, so they'll be late. The Bijan al-Gaib picks in 2028 and 2029 are the lottery tickets. Don't touch anything. Lose with dignity. Or without it. Either works.

5.head: 2-8 · Elo 1238 (12th) · WAR pace -0.74 (11th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
5.headline: Eight First-Round Picks and One Game Left That Matters
5.text: The 'Doza won last week with 56.18 points. That's the eighth-lowest score in league history and it was a win, because Baby Billys scored 53.84. I followed that game the way you watch a car back into a mailbox. Both wins this year are against the other two teams in the basement. The best lineup available is on pace for -0.74 WAR and has three tight ends in it, with Darren Waller in the superflex. The team is named after Fernando Mendoza, who has banked -0.69 WAR in ten games. Rookie quarterbacks take time. I get it. It's still a tough look for the letterhead. None of that is the point. The point is eight first-round picks in three drafts: four in 2027, three in 2028, one in 2029. But two things changed. Baby Billys has eight firsts now too, so this isn't the only war chest in the league anymore. And the 2027 firsts from Drake Mungo, the Cockroach and MOORE keep sliding later, because those three keep winning. So the biggest game left is Week 13 against MOORE. Draft order goes by max points, not record, so winning it (9% to happen) costs nothing and helps keep MOORE's pick in the lottery. Root accordingly.

12.head: 1-9 · Elo 1295 (10th) · WAR pace +1.12 (10th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
12.headline: A Rebuild on a One-Year Clock
12.text: Two weeks ago I asked for one thing: grab a warm-body quarterback so the superflex isn't a tight end. The Tenders started Tua Tagovailoa last week. He scored 0.0. That's not a warm body. That's a body. It's 1-9, 12-98 in all-play, and the best lineup still has three tight ends in it. Baker Mayfield is below replacement for the season, Jaxson Dart had knee surgery in September and is out for the rest of the regular season, and Brian Thomas, the centerpiece of the Saquon trade, has banked -0.40 WAR and sits behind Ryan Flournoy. Fine. Nobody's here for 2026. The draft board is the good news: its own 2027 first, currently second in the race for the 1.01, plus the Nix pics' first, which gets better every week they lose (and they've lost five of six). Harold Fannin, fifth among tight ends in WAR pace at 22, is a keeper. Here's the bad news nobody's talking about: the 2028 first belongs to Drake Mungo. This rebuild is on a one-year clock. Two picks that could both land in the top six have to hit right away, because being bad again in 2027 just hands Drake Mungo a lottery ticket. Collect seconds, hit on the picks, and for the love of God, start a quarterback.
